scope: Chapters 0–10; normalized exact term matching (case, whitespace, Unicode compatibility); not a synonym audit

model.definition: representation of something that is often too difficult (or impossible) to display directly
simplified description that contains only those elements necessary to describe the physics of a physical situation

meter.definition: the SI unit for length, abbreviated (m)

common application of magnetic torque on a current-carrying loop that is very similar in construction to a motor; by design, the torque is proportional to I and not θ, so the needle deflection is proportional to the current

vector.definition: a quantity that is described by both magnitude and direction
a quantity with both magnitude and direction

acceleration.definition: the rate of change in velocity; the change in velocity over time
the rate at which an object’s velocity changes over a period of time

free-fall.definition: the state of movement that results from gravitational force only
a situation in which the only force acting on an object is the force due to gravity

mechanical energy.definition: the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy
sum of the kinetic energy and potential energy of a system; this sum is a constant

ohm’s law.definition: an empirical relation stating that the current I is proportional to the potential difference V. It is often written as I = V/R, where R is the resistance
the relationship between current, voltage, and resistance within an electrical circuit: V=IR

resistance.definition: the electric property that impedes current; for ohmic materials, it is the ratio of voltage to current, R = V/I
causing a loss of electrical power in a circuit
